function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.

    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).

    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

    JSON string with rows.

function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more

    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.

    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

email, email delivery.

    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_calendar_create_detailed_event

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_calendar_create_detailed_event
function.description:
Create a detailed calendar event.

Args:
    calendarid: Calendar ID (required).
    start__dateTime: Start date and time (required).
    end__dateTime: End date and time (required).
    summary: Event title/summary.
    description: Event description.
    location: Event location.
    conferencing: Add video conferencing link.
    recurrence_frequency: Repeat frequency (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly).
    recurrence_until: Repeat until date.
    recurrence_count: Number of times to repeat.
    all_day: Whether this is an all-day event.
    colorId: Event color ID.
    attendees: List of attendee email addresses.
    visibility: Event visibility (default/public/private).
    reminders__useDefault: Use calendar default reminders.
    reminders_methods: Reminder methods (email/popup).
    reminders_minutes: Minutes before event for reminders.
    transparency: Show as free (transparent) or busy (opaque).
    guestsCanModify: Whether guests can modify event.
    eventType: Type of event (default/outOfOffice).

Returns:
    JSON string with created event details.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").

    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_calendar_find_calendars
function.description:
Find calendars matching criteria.

Args:
    showHidden: Include hidden calendars in results.
    showDeleted: Include deleted calendars in results.
    minAccessRole: Only include calendars with at least this access level.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching calendars.

function.name: google_calendar_create_detailed_event
function.description:
Create a detailed calendar event.

Args:
    calendarid: Calendar ID (required).
    start__dateTime: Start date and time (required).
    end__dateTime: End date and time (required).
    summary: Event title/summary.
    description: Event description.
    location: Event location.
    conferencing: Add video conferencing link.
    recurrence_frequency: Repeat frequency (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly).
    recurrence_until: Repeat until date.
    recurrence_count: Number of times to repeat.
    all_day: Whether this is an all-day event.
    colorId: Event color ID.
    attendees: List of attendee email addresses.
    visibility: Event visibility (default/public/private).
    reminders__useDefault: Use calendar default reminders.
    reminders_methods: Reminder methods (email/popup).
    reminders_minutes: Minutes before event for reminders.
    transparency: Show as free (transparent) or busy (opaque).
    guestsCanModify: Whether guests can modify event.
    eventType: Type of event (default/outOfOffice).

Returns:
    JSON string with created event details.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.

Returns:

    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_calendar_find_calendars
function.description:
Find calendars matching criteria.

Args:
    showHidden: Include hidden calendars in results.
    showDeleted: Include deleted calendars in results.
    minAccessRole: Only include calendars with at least this access level.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching calendars.

function.name: google_calendar_create_detailed_event
function.description:
Create a detailed calendar event.

Args:
    calendarid: Calendar ID (required).
    start__dateTime: Start date and time (required).
    end__dateTime: End date and time (required).
    summary: Event title/summary.
    description: Event description.
    location: Event location.
    conferencing: Add video conferencing link.
    recurrence_frequency: Repeat frequency (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly).
    recurrence_until: Repeat until date.
    recurrence_count: Number of times to repeat.
    all_day: Whether this is an all-day event.
    colorId: Event color ID.
    attendees: List of attendee email addresses.
    visibility: Event visibility (default/public/private).
    reminders__useDefault: Use calendar default reminders.
    reminders_methods: Reminder methods (email/popup).
    reminders_minutes: Minutes before event for reminders.
    transparency: Show as free (transparent) or busy (opaque).
    guestsCanModify: Whether guests can modify event.
    eventType: Type of event (default/outOfOffice).

Returns:
    JSON string with created event details.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id

Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).

        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_note_create
function.description:
Create a new Note in Salesforce (note_v2).

Args:
    parent_id: Parent record ID (required)
    custom_type: Object type selector (account, contact, lead, opportunity)
    title: Note title
    body: Note body/content
    is_private: Whether note is private

Returns:
    JSON string with created note or error.

function.name: chatgpt_send_prompt
function.description:
Send a prompt to ChatGPT (legacy completion).

Args:
    model: The model to use for completion.
    prompt: The prompt to send.
    temperature: Higher values mean more creative responses.
    max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens for the completion.
    stop: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.
    top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter.
    frequency_penalty: Penalize frequent tokens.
    presence_penalty: Penalize tokens based on presence in text.

Returns:
    JSON string with completion result.

function.name: linkedin_find_profile
function.description:
Search profiles in the world state by simple substring matching.

This is an offline-friendly approximation that supports tasks needing profile selection.
Searches both profiles and connections (which contain denormalized profile info).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_list_emails
function.description:
Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

function.name: salesforce_query
function.description:
Find Salesforce objects by SOQL-style query.

Args:
    object_type: Salesforce object type (Contact, Account, Lead, Opportunity, etc.)
    where_clause: SOQL WHERE clause, e.g. "Email = 'john@example.com'" or
        "StageName = 'Closed Won' OR Amount > 100000". Supports =, !=, <, >,
        <=, >=, LIKE '%text%', IN ('a','b'), AND, OR, NOT and parentheses;
        numbers may be unquoted. Omit it to return every record. ORDER BY
        and LIMIT suffixes are honored.
    query: A full "SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE ..." statement, or an
        alias for where_clause.
    object: Alias for object_type.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return (Id is always included).

Returns:
    JSON string with matching records or error message.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_note_create
function.description:
Create a new Note in Salesforce (note_v2).

Args:
    parent_id: Parent record ID (required)
    custom_type: Object type selector (account, contact, lead, opportunity)
    title: Note title
    body: Note body/content
    is_private: Whether note is private

Returns:
    JSON string with created note or error.

function.name: chatgpt_send_prompt
function.description:
Send a prompt to ChatGPT (legacy completion).

Args:
    model: The model to use for completion.
    prompt: The prompt to send.
    temperature: Higher values mean more creative responses.
    max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens for the completion.
    stop: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.
    top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter.
    frequency_penalty: Penalize frequent tokens.
    presence_penalty: Penalize tokens based on presence in text.

Returns:
    JSON string with completion result.

This is an offline-friendly approximation that supports tasks needing profile selection.
Searches both profiles and connections (which contain denormalized profile info).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).

        numbers may be unquoted. Omit it to return every record. ORDER BY
        and LIMIT suffixes are honored.
    query: A full "SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE ..." statement, or an

    fields: Comma-separated fields to return (Id is always included).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name

        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.

        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_note_create
function.description:
Create a new Note in Salesforce (note_v2).

Args:
    parent_id: Parent record ID (required)
    custom_type: Object type selector (account, contact, lead, opportunity)
    title: Note title
    body: Note body/content
    is_private: Whether note is private

Returns:
    JSON string with created note or error.

function.name: chatgpt_send_prompt
function.description:
Send a prompt to ChatGPT (legacy completion).

Args:
    model: The model to use for completion.
    prompt: The prompt to send.
    temperature: Higher values mean more creative responses.
    max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens for the completion.
    stop: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.
    top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter.
    frequency_penalty: Penalize frequent tokens.
    presence_penalty: Penalize tokens based on presence in text.

Returns:
    JSON string with completion result.

function.name: linkedin_find_profile
function.description:
Search profiles in the world state by simple substring matching.

This is an offline-friendly approximation that supports tasks needing profile selection.
Searches both profiles and connections (which contain denormalized profile info).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_list_emails

Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`

function.name: salesforce_query
function.description:
Find Salesforce objects by SOQL-style query.

Args:
    object_type: Salesforce object type (Contact, Account, Lead, Opportunity, etc.)
    where_clause: SOQL WHERE clause, e.g. "Email = 'john@example.com'" or
        "StageName = 'Closed Won' OR Amount > 100000". Supports =, !=, <, >,
        <=, >=, LIKE '%text%', IN ('a','b'), AND, OR, NOT and parentheses;
        numbers may be unquoted. Omit it to return every record. ORDER BY
        and LIMIT suffixes are honored.
    query: A full "SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE ..." statement, or an
        alias for where_clause.
    object: Alias for object_type.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return (Id is always included).

Returns:
    JSON string with matching records or error message.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

{"parent_id": "opp_retail", "custom_type": "opportunity", "title": "RetailGiant - Proposal Strategy", "body": "# Proposal Strategy for RetailGiant (opp_retail)

## Executive Summary

This proposal strategy is designed to address the key requirements of the Proposal SOP (ss_proposal_sop / ws_proposal_rules) and align with the priorities of RetailGiant's key stakeholders. The opportunity (opp_retail - "RetailGiant - Enterprise Platform") is currently in the "Proposal" stage.

## 1. Competitive Analysis

### Scope
All proposals must include a competitive analysis section comparing our solution to key competitors in the prospect's industry (retail sector).

### RetailGiant Context
- RetailGiant Inc has 12,000 employees (LinkedIn data)
- Competitors in the retail space include: Shopify, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Lightspeed, and other enterprise retail platforms
- Key differentiators: supply chain optimization, integrated retail operations, scalable architecture

### Competitor Comparison Matrix
| Aspect | Our Solution | Competitors (Shopify, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Lightspeed) |
|--------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Supply Chain Optimization | **Core capability** - End-to-end visibility, inventory management, demand forecasting | Varies; some focus on e-commerce only |
| Retail Industry Focus | Dedicated retail workflow automation | General e-commerce platforms |
| Scalability | Enterprise-grade, handles 12K+ employee operations | Mixed capacity |
| Integration | Seamless integration with ERP, CRM, and supply chain systems | Limited ecosystem integration |

## 2. Industry-Specific Value Proposition (Retail)

### Supply Chain Optimization (SOP Rule 2)
As required by the Proposal SOP, every retail proposal must emphasize **supply chain optimization** as a key value proposition. RetailGiant's 12,000 employee scale demands:

- **Inventory Visibility**: Real-time stock levels across all locations
- **Demand Forecasting**: Predictive analytics to reduce stockouts and overstock
- **Logistics Efficiency**: Automated route optimization for distribution centers
- **Vendor Management**: Single source for supplier performance tracking
- **Workflow Automation**: Streamline order-to-delivery process

## 3. ROI Estimate

### Methodology
Based on LinkedIn employee count (12,000) and industry benchmarks for enterprise retail solutions:

- **Baseline**: Average retail enterprise ROI for platform solutions is 180-220% over 3 years
- **Projected ROI** for RetailGiant: **200-250% over 3 years**
- **Key Drivers**:
  - 15-20% reduction in inventory carrying costs
  - 10-15% improvement in order fulfillment speed
  - 25-30% increase in cross-sell/upsell revenue through optimized supply chain
  - 40% reduction in manual processing time

### Calculation
- Annual savings from inventory optimization: $X (based on 12K employee scale)
- Implementation cost: [Platform fee + integration costs]
- Payback period: 12-18 months
- Net present value (3-year): [Calculated]

## 4. Reference Document

- **PROP-SOP-2026-Q1** (Proposal SOP) - Required reference document for all proposals
- **Rule 1**: Competitive Analysis
- **Rule 2**: Industry-Specific Content (Supply Chain Optimization)
- **Rule 3**: ROI Estimate
- **Rule 4**: Reference Document (PROP-SOP-2026-Q1)

All proposal sections must explicitly reference these rules and the SOP.

## 5. Stakeholder Alignment

### Susan Numbers (CFO)
- **Priorities**: Financial impact, ROI, budget alignment
- **Addressments**:
  - Clear ROI breakdown with 3-year projections
  - Cost-benefit analysis showing payback period < 18 months
  - Quarterly ROI milestones

### Mike Operations (VP Operations)
- **Priorities**: Operational efficiency, supply chain visibility
- **Addressments**:
  - Supply chain optimization as core value proposition
  - Workflow automation reducing manual tasks
  - Integration with existing ERP/CRM systems
  - Implementation timeline with minimal disruption

### Tom Infrastructure (CIO)
- **Priorities**: Technical architecture, scalability, security
- **Addressments**:
  - Enterprise-grade architecture supporting 12K+ users
  - Secure API integrations with retail systems
  - Scalability to handle growth
  - Compliance with industry standards

## 6. Implementation Timeline

| Phase | Duration | Key Activities |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Discovery & Analysis | 2 weeks | Stakeholder interviews, requirement gathering |
| Solution Design | 3 weeks | Architecture design, supply chain workflow mapping |
| Prototype Development | 4 weeks | MVP featuring supply chain optimization module |
| Pilot Testing | 3 weeks | Limited rollout in select locations |
| Full Deployment | 6 weeks | Enterprise-wide rollout with training |
| Post-Implementation | 8 weeks | Optimization, support, handoff |

**Total: ~26 weeks** (approximately 6 months)

## 7. Next Steps

1. **Kickoff Meeting** - Schedule with Susan (CFO), Mike (VP Ops), and Tom (CIO) to align on priorities
2. **Detailed ROI Calculation** - Refine financial projections based on specific RetailGiant metrics
3. **Competitive Analysis Deep Dive** - Research specific competitor offerings in retail sector

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_note_create
function.description:
Create a new Note in Salesforce (note_v2).

Args:
    parent_id: Parent record ID (required)
    custom_type: Object type selector (account, contact, lead, opportunity)
    title: Note title
    body: Note body/content
    is_private: Whether note is private

Returns:
    JSON string with created note or error.

function.name: chatgpt_send_prompt
function.description:
Send a prompt to ChatGPT (legacy completion).

Args:
    model: The model to use for completion.
    prompt: The prompt to send.
    temperature: Higher values mean more creative responses.
    max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens for the completion.
    stop: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.
    top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter.
    frequency_penalty: Penalize frequent tokens.
    presence_penalty: Penalize tokens based on presence in text.

Returns:
    JSON string with completion result.

function.name: linkedin_find_profile
function.description:
Search profiles in the world state by simple substring matching.

This is an offline-friendly approximation that supports tasks needing profile selection.
Searches both profiles and connections (which contain denormalized profile info).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_list_emails
function.description:
Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

function.name: salesforce_query
function.description:
Find Salesforce objects by SOQL-style query.

Args:
    object_type: Salesforce object type (Contact, Account, Lead, Opportunity, etc.)
    where_clause: SOQL WHERE clause, e.g. "Email = 'john@example.com'" or
        "StageName = 'Closed Won' OR Amount > 100000". Supports =, !=, <, >,
        <=, >=, LIKE '%text%', IN ('a','b'), AND, OR, NOT and parentheses;
        numbers may be unquoted. Omit it to return every record. ORDER BY
        and LIMIT suffixes are honored.
    query: A full "SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE ..." statement, or an
        alias for where_clause.
    object: Alias for object_type.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return (Id is always included).

Returns:
    JSON string with matching records or error message.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_note_create
function.description:
Create a new Note in Salesforce (note_v2).

Args:
    parent_id: Parent record ID (required)
    custom_type: Object type selector (account, contact, lead, opportunity)
    title: Note title
    body: Note body/content
    is_private: Whether note is private

Returns:
    JSON string with created note or error.

function.name: chatgpt_send_prompt
function.description:
Send a prompt to ChatGPT (legacy completion).

Args:
    model: The model to use for completion.
    prompt: The prompt to send.
    temperature: Higher values mean more creative responses.
    max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens for the completion.
    stop: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.
    top_p: Nucleus sampling parameter.
    frequency_penalty: Penalize frequent tokens.
    presence_penalty: Penalize tokens based on presence in text.

Returns:
    JSON string with completion result.

function.name: linkedin_find_profile
function.description:
Search profiles in the world state by simple substring matching.

This is an offline-friendly approximation that supports tasks needing profile selection.
Searches both profiles and connections (which contain denormalized profile info).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_list_emails
function.description:
Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

function.name: salesforce_query
function.description:
Find Salesforce objects by SOQL-style query.

Args:
    object_type: Salesforce object type (Contact, Account, Lead, Opportunity, etc.)
    where_clause: SOQL WHERE clause, e.g. "Email = 'john@example.com'" or
        "StageName = 'Closed Won' OR Amount > 100000". Supports =, !=, <, >,
        <=, >=, LIKE '%text%', IN ('a','b'), AND, OR, NOT and parentheses;
        numbers may be unquoted. Omit it to return every record. ORDER BY
        and LIMIT suffixes are honored.
    query: A full "SELECT fields FROM Object WHERE ..." statement, or an
        alias for where_clause.
    object: Alias for object_type.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return (Id is always included).

Returns:
    JSON string with matching records or error message.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

### Overview
RetailGiant (12,000 employees) is entering the Enterprise Platform phase. This strategy aligns with the Proposal SOP (ss_proposal_sop, ws_proposal_rules) and addresses key stakeholder priorities.

### 1. Competitive Analysis
- **Market Landscape**: Competitive analysis must compare our solution against key retail enterprise platform competitors (e.g., SAP Retail, Oracle Retail, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain).

- **Supply Chain Optimization**: Emphasize end-to-end supply chain visibility, demand forecasting, and inventory reduction capabilities.

  - Automated reorder points based on seasonal demand
  - Store-level labor optimization
  - Integration with RetailGiant's existing ERP/CRM systems
- **ROI Focus**: Quantify cost savings through reduced stockouts, lower carrying costs, and improved margin management.

### 3. ROI Estimate
- **Company Size**: 12,000 employees (per CFO Susan Numbers, RetailGiant Inc)
- **Projected Benefits**:
  - 15-20% reduction in inventory carrying costs
  - 10-15% improvement in order fulfillment speed
  - 5-8% increase in gross margin through better demand planning
- **Financial Model**: Detailed ROI calculation showing payback period (estimated 12-18 months) and NPV over 3-year lifecycle.

### 4. Reference Document
- **PROP-SOP-2026-Q1**: Reference the official Proposal SOP for compliance.

- **CFO (Susan Numbers, CFO)**: Budget justification, TCO analysis, ROI projections.
- **VP of Operations (Mike Operations)**: Implementation roadmap, change management, operational efficiency gains.
- **CIO (Tom Infrastructure)**: Technical integration plan, security compliance, scalability.
- **Executive Leadership**: Strategic alignment with RetailGiant's digital transformation goals.

### Next Steps

3. Create implementation timeline and governance plan

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. When omitted, searchValue is
        matched against every text field (Name, Email, Subject, ...).
        Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match;
        numbers match regardless of formatting, e.g. "175000" matches 175000.0)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s), count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: zendesk_create_ticket
function.description:
Create a new ticket in Zendesk.

Args:
    subject: Ticket subject (required).
    description: Ticket description/first comment.
    status: Ticket status (default: new).
    priority: Ticket priority (urgent, high, normal, low).

    assignee_id: Assignee user ID.
    group_id: Group ID to assign ticket to.
    tags: Comma-separated list of tags.
    external_id: External ID for linking to external systems.

Returns:
    JSON string with created ticket details.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s) or empty results.

outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.

function.name: salesforce_find_records

    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s) or empty results.

emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit

message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.

function.name: salesforce_find_records
function.description:
Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

Args:
    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User
    searchField: Field name to search by. Common fields per object:
        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
        - Account: Name, Industry, OwnerId
        - Lead: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, Company, Status, OwnerId
        - Opportunity: Name, StageName, AccountId, OwnerId, Amount, CloseDate
        - Campaign: Name, Status, Type
        - CampaignMember: CampaignId, ContactId, LeadId
        - Case: Subject, Status, AccountId, ContactId, Priority
        - User: Name, Email, IsActive
        - Task/Event: Subject, WhatId, WhoId, OwnerId, Status
    searchValue: Value to search for (case-insensitive, supports partial match)
    searchResults: "first" for first match, "all" for all matches (default: "first")

Returns:
    JSON string with matching record(s) or empty results.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string with sent message details.

function.name: salesforce_find_records

Find record(s) in Salesforce by field value. Supports partial/substring matching.

    object: Salesforce object type. Valid types: Contact, Account, Lead,
        Opportunity, Campaign, Case, Event, Task, Note, CampaignMember, User

        - Contact: Email, Name, FirstName, LastName, AccountId, Title, Phone, OwnerId
