function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

function.name: google_sheets_lookup_row
function.description:
Find rows whose lookup column equals a value.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). This simulation does not
create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows, result_count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_add_row
function.description:
Create a new row in a spreadsheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    timezone: Use spreadsheet timezone for date formatting.
    cells: JSON object of column name to value pairs, e.g. '{"Name": "John", "Age": "30"}',
        or a list of values in the worksheet's column order.
    values: Alias for cells.

Returns:
    JSON string with the created row (row_id and cells), or an error when the
    spreadsheet or worksheet does not exist.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:

function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

function.name: google_sheets_lookup_row
function.description:
Find rows whose lookup column equals a value.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). This simulation does not
create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows, result_count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: reamaze_get_conversations
function.description:
Get all conversations from Re:amaze.

Returns:
    JSON string with all conversations.

function.name: reamaze_update_conversation
function.description:
Update an existing conversation in Re:amaze.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation ID to update (required).
    status: New status.
    category: New category.
    tags: Comma-separated list of tags (replaces existing).
    assignee_email: Email of the agent to assign this conversation to.

Returns:
    JSON string with updated conversation details.

function.name: reamaze_add_message
function.description:
Add a message to an existing conversation.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation ID to add message to.
    body: The message body.
    author_type: Author type (customer or staff).
    author_email: Author email.
    author_name: Author name.
    visibility: Message visibility (regular or internal).

Returns:
    JSON string with result.

function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

function.name: google_sheets_lookup_row
function.description:
Find rows whose lookup column equals a value.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). This simulation does not
create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows, result_count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_add_row
function.description:
Create a new row in a spreadsheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    timezone: Use spreadsheet timezone for date formatting.
    cells: JSON object of column name to value pairs, e.g. '{"Name": "John", "Age": "30"}',
        or a list of values in the worksheet's column order.
    values: Alias for cells.

Returns:
    JSON string with the created row (row_id and cells), or an error when the
    spreadsheet or worksheet does not exist.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: slack_send_channel_message
function.description:
Send a message to a Slack channel.

Args:
    channel: Channel ID or name.
    text: Message text.
    add_app_to_channel: Whether to auto-add Zapier app to channel (default True).
    as_bot: Whether to send as a bot (default True).
    username: Bot name to use (if sending as bot).
    icon: Bot icon (URL or emoji like :robot_face:).
    add_edit_link: Whether to include link to this Zap (default True).
    image_url: URL of image to attach.
    unfurl: Whether to auto-expand links (default True).
    link_names: Whether to link @mentions (default True).
    post_at: Schedule message for later (ISO datetime).
    thread_ts: Parent message timestamp if replying to a thread.
    reply_broadcast: Also send thread reply to channel (default False).

Returns:
    JSON string with sent message details.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: slack_list_channels
function.description:
List all channels available to the user.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet

Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: reamaze_get_conversations
function.description:
Get all conversations from Re:amaze.

Returns:
    JSON string with all conversations.

function.name: reamaze_update_conversation
function.description:
Update an existing conversation in Re:amaze.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation ID to update (required).
    status: New status.
    category: New category.
    tags: Comma-separated list of tags (replaces existing).
    assignee_email: Email of the agent to assign this conversation to.

Returns:
    JSON string with updated conversation details.

function.name: reamaze_add_message
function.description:
Add a message to an existing conversation.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation ID to add message to.
    body: The message body.
    author_type: Author type (customer or staff).
    author_email: Author email.
    author_name: Author name.
    visibility: Message visibility (regular or internal).

Returns:
    JSON string with result.

function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

function.name: google_sheets_lookup_row
function.description:
Find rows whose lookup column equals a value.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). This simulation does not
create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows, result_count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_add_row
function.description:
Create a new row in a spreadsheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    timezone: Use spreadsheet timezone for date formatting.
    cells: JSON object of column name to value pairs, e.g. '{"Name": "John", "Age": "30"}',
        or a list of values in the worksheet's column order.
    values: Alias for cells.

Returns:
    JSON string with the created row (row_id and cells), or an error when the
    spreadsheet or worksheet does not exist.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.

function.name: google_sheets_find_many_rows
function.description:
Find multiple rows matching lookup criteria.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). Without any criteria every
row matches. row_count limits the rows returned after filtering;
total_count reports how many rows matched.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.
    col_name: Alias for lookup_key.
    filters: Extra column conditions, e.g. {"Status": "Open"}.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows.

function.name: google_sheets_lookup_row
function.description:
Find rows whose lookup column equals a value.

Matching ignores case, surrounding whitespace, a leading "#" and number
formatting ("4511" matches "#4511" and 4511.0). This simulation does not
create a row when nothing matches; use google_sheets_add_row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    lookup_key: Column to search in (required).
    lookup_value: Value to search for (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    lookup_key_support: Secondary column to search in.
    lookup_value_support: Secondary value to search for.
    bottom_up: Search from bottom of spreadsheet up.
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching rows, result_count returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_update_row
function.description:
Update a spreadsheet row.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    row: Row ID to update, as returned in a row's row_id (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    background_color: Background color for the row.
    text_color: Text color for the row.
    text_format_bold: Bold text formatting (unchanged when omitted).
    text_format_italic: Italic text formatting (unchanged when omitted).
    text_format_strikethrough: Strikethrough text formatting (unchanged when omitted).
    cells: JSON object of column name to value pairs to update, e.g. '{"Name": "Jane"}',
        or a list of values in the worksheet's column order.

Returns:
    JSON string with updated row details.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id
function.description:
Get a specific email by its message ID.

Args:
    message_id: The unique ID of the email message to retrieve.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal").

Returns:
    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; AND binds more tightly than OR; parentheses group expressions.
        Quoted phrases stay together. Brace/field-scoped groups are unsupported.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id
function.description:
Get a specific email by its message ID.

Args:
    message_id: The unique ID of the email message to retrieve.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal").

Returns:
    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: gmail_list_emails

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string with sent message details.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string with sent message details.

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, subject:,
        label:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred, has:attachment, OR, and
        plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread").
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id
function.description:
Get a specific email by its message ID.

Args:
    message_id: The unique ID of the email message to retrieve.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal").

Returns:
    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: gmail_list_emails
function.description:
Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns to include (e.g., "A:Z") (required).
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return (required).
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: Output format (all/rows/raw_rows/formatted_rows).
    first_row: First row to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

Returns:

    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID (required).

function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").

    JSON string with sent message details.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id
function.description:
Get a specific email by its message ID.

Args:
    message_id: The unique ID of the email message to retrieve.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal").

Returns:
    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: gmail_list_emails
function.description:
Alias for `gmail_find_email`.

Some tasks refer to a "list" operation; in our environment `gmail_find_email`
already returns a list of matching messages.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id
function.description:
Get a specific email by its message ID.

Args:
    message_id: The unique ID of the email message to retrieve.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal").

Returns:
    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: google_sheets_get_many_rows
function.description:
Get multiple rows from a worksheet.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    worksheet: Worksheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    worksheet_id: Alias for worksheet.
    range: Columns (and optionally rows) to include, e.g. "A:Z" or "A2:C40".
    row_count: Maximum number of rows to return; total_count and has_more
        report whether more rows exist.
    drive: Google Drive location.
    output_format: "raw_rows" returns headers plus value lists; any other
        value (all/rows/formatted_rows) returns column-name objects.
    first_row: First row number to retrieve.

Returns:
    JSON string with rows.

function.name: google_drive_find_multiple_files
function.description:
Find files (including Google Sheets spreadsheets) in Google Drive by name.

Args:
    title: Text to find in file names (case-insensitive). Files whose name
        contains every word are returned first; if none do, files matching
        some of the words are returned ranked by matches with
        ``partial_match: true``. Omit to list all files.
    info: Alias for title.
    search_type: Zapier search type (accepted for compatibility).
    drive: Google Drive location (accepted for compatibility).
    folder: Only return files known to be in this folder ID.
    file_types: Only return these MIME types, e.g.
        "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet" or "spreadsheet".
    max_results: Maximum number of files to return (default 25).

Returns:
    JSON with ``results`` (id, title, mimeType), ``count`` returned and
    ``total_count`` matching. An empty list means no file matched.

function.name: google_sheets_get_spreadsheet_by_id
function.description:
Get a spreadsheet and its worksheets by ID or title.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    includeGridData: Also return each worksheet's first 20 rows (row_id and
        cells) with its total row_count. Use google_sheets_get_many_rows or
        google_sheets_find_many_rows for more rows.

Returns:
    JSON string with spreadsheet details and worksheets (id, title, headers).

function.name: google_sheets_find_worksheet
function.description:
Find a worksheet by title (or ID) in a spreadsheet.

Titles match case-insensitively. When spreadsheet is omitted, the
worksheet is looked up across all spreadsheets and returned if unique.

Args:
    spreadsheet: Spreadsheet ID or title (required).
    title: Worksheet title (or ID) to search for (required).
    spreadsheet_id: Alias for spreadsheet.
    drive: Google Drive location.

Returns:
    JSON string with matching worksheet.

Let me analyze the data I've retrieved:

**Q1 Budget Tracker (ss_budget)** has 4 worksheets:
1. **ws_spend** (Actuals vs Plan) - Contains department spending data
2. **ws_amendments** (Budget Amendments) - Contains amendment data
3. **ws_policy** (Budget Policy) - Contains policy rules
4. **ws_contacts** (Dept Contacts) - Contains department contacts

**From ws_spend (Actuals vs Plan):**
- Engineering: Software Licenses - Budget $50,000, Actual $58,000 (over by $8,000)
- Engineering: Hardware - Budget $30,000, Actual $33,500 (over by $3,500)
- Marketing: Advertising - Budget $80,000, Actual $92,000 (over by $12,000)
- Marketing: Events - Budget $25,000, Actual $27,500 (over by $2,500)
- Sales: Travel - Budget $40,000, Actual $48,000 (over by $8,000)
- Sales: Client Entertainment - Budget $15,000, Actual $16,500 (over by $1,500)
- HR: Training - Budget $20,000, Actual $22,000 (over by $2,000)
- Engineering: Cloud Infrastructure - Budget $45,000, Actual $44,800 (under by $200)

**From ws_amendments (Budget Amendments):**
- Engineering - Software Licenses - Adjustment +$5,000 - Approved - 2026-01-15
- Marketing - Events - Adjustment +$3,000 - Approved - 2026-01-20
- Sales - Travel - Adjustment +$2,000 - Rejected - 2026-01-22
- Engineering - Hardware - Adjustment +$3,000 - Pending - 2026-02-05
- Sales - Travel - Adjustment +$10,000 - Approved - 2026-01-28 but "amendment voided per CFO directive REV-2026-003"

**From ws_policy (Budget Policy):**
- Variance Threshold: 10% - Flag line items where actual exceeds adjusted budget by more than this percentage
- Amendment Eligibility: Only apply amendments with Approved status
- Voided Amendment Handling: Amendments with void/revocation references must not be applied

**From ws_contacts (Dept Contacts):**
- Engineering: eng.head@ourcompany.example.com
- Marketing: mkt.head@ourcompany.example.com
- Sales: sales.head@ourcompany.example.com
- HR: hr.head@ourcompany.example.com

Now I need to calculate variances and identify which departments exceeded their adjusted budget by more than the 10% threshold.

Let me calculate the variances:

**Engineering:**
- Software Licenses: Budget $50,000, Actual $58,000 → Over by $8,000. Variance % = $8,000 / $50,000 = 16% > 10% threshold → **OVER**
- Hardware: Budget $30,000, Actual $33,500 → Over by $3,500. Variance % = $3,500 / $30,000 = 11.67% > 10% threshold → **OVER**
- Cloud Infrastructure: Budget $45,000, Actual $44,800 → Under by $200. Variance % = -$200/$45,000 = -0.44% → OK

**Marketing:**
- Advertising: Budget $80,000, Actual $92,000 → Over by $12,000. Variance % = $12,000 / $80,000 = 15% > 10% threshold → **OVER**
- Events: Budget $25,000, Actual $27,500 → Over by $2,500. Variance % = $2,500 / $25,000 = 10% → Exactly 10%, not exceeding → **NOT OVER** (needs to exceed threshold)

**Sales:**
- Travel: Budget $40,000, Actual $48,000 → Over by $8,000. Variance % = $8,000 / $40,000 = 20% > 10% threshold → **OVER**
- Client Entertainment: Budget $15,000, Actual $16,500 → Over by $1,500. Variance % = $1,500 / $15,000 = 10% → Exactly 10%, not exceeding → **NOT OVER**

**HR:**
- Training: Budget $20,000, Actual $22,000 → Over by $2,000. Variance % = $2,000 / $20,000 = 10% → Exactly 10%, not exceeding → **NOT OVER**

So the departments that exceeded the 10% threshold are:
1. **Engineering** - Software Licenses (16% over), Hardware (11.67% over)
2. **Marketing** - Advertising (15% over)
3. **Sales** - Travel (20% over)

The Engineering department has two line items over budget. The CFO wants to know about overruns exceeding the variance threshold.

I need to:
1. Flag these departments (Engineering, Marketing, Sales) with their overages
2. Send notifications to the relevant department heads (using the contact emails from ws_contacts)
3. Post a heads-up to the finance alerts Slack channel (CFA)

Let me send emails to the department heads and a Slack message to the finance-alerts channel.

Department heads:
- Engineering: eng.head@ourcompany.example.com
- Marketing: mkt.head@ourcompany.example.com
- Sales: sales.head@ourcompany.example.com
- HR: hr.head@ourcompany.example.com

I'll send emails to Engineering, Marketing, and Sales heads (since HR is not over budget). Actually, let me also include HR for completeness since the finance team might want to know the full picture. But the instruction says "flag anything where a department went significantly over their adjusted budget" - so I should focus on the ones that actually exceeded.

Let me send the notifications and Slack message.

messages.content:
The reconciliation is complete. Here's a summary of the findings and actions taken:

## Q1 Budget Reconciliation - Results

**Policy Threshold:** 10% variance (from `ws_policy`)

**Departments with overruns exceeding the 10% threshold:**

| Department | Line Item | Budget | Actual | Overage | Variance |
|------------|-----------|--------|--------|---------|----------|
| **Engineering** | Software Licenses | $50,000 | $58,000 | $8,000 | 16% |
| **Engineering** | Hardware | $30,000 | $33,500 | $3,500 | 11.67% |
| **Marketing** | Advertising | $80,000 | $92,000 | $12,000 | 15% |
| **Sales** | Travel | $40,000 | $48,000 | $8,000 | 20% |

**Key Notes:**
- **Engineering Hardware** amendment (+$3,000) was pending at data pull but still exceeds the 10% threshold (11.67%).
- **Marketing Advertising** ($12,000 over, 15%) and **Sales Travel** ($8,000 over, 20%) are the most significant overruns.
- **Sales Travel** had an approved amendment (+$2,000 on 2026-01-28) but was **voided per CFO directive REV-2026-003** — excluded per policy "Voided Amendment Handling."
- All four departments (Engineering, Marketing, Sales, HR) have contact information in `ws_contacts`. HR was not flagged as over budget.

**Actions Taken:**

1. **Emails sent** to department heads:
   - **Engineering** (eng.head@ourcompany.example.com) – Software Licenses & Hardware overruns
   - **Marketing** (mkt.head@ourcompany.example.com) – Advertising overrun
   - **Sales** (sales.head@ourcompany.example.com) – Travel overrun

2. **Slack alert posted** to `CFA` (finance-alerts) with full details and source references.

All notifications have been delivered successfully. The CFO will receive the heads-up and the department leads have been directed to provide updated plans or approval for the overruns.
messages.reasoning_content:
All three emails and the Slack message have been sent successfully. Let me verify the results:

1. **Engineering** - Software Licenses: $50,000 budget vs $58,000 actual (16% over) - OVER
2. **Engineering** - Hardware: $30,000 budget vs $33,500 actual (11.67% over) - OVER
3. **Marketing** - Advertising: $80,000 budget vs $92,000 actual (15% over) - OVER
4. **Sales** - Travel: $40,000 budget vs $48,000 actual (20% over) - OVER

The Policy (ws_policy) states:
- Variance Threshold: 10%
- Amendment Eligibility: Only apply amendments with Approved status
- Voided Amendment Handling: Exclude from adjustments (amendments with void/revocation references must not be applied)

The amendments that were approved:
- Engineering - Software Licenses: +$5,000 (Approved, 2026-01-15)
- Marketing - Events: +$3,000 (Approved, 2026-01-20)
- Sales - Travel: +$2,000 (Approved, 2026-01-28) - BUT this was voided per CFO directive REV-2026-003

The Sales Travel amendment was approved but then voided per CFO directive, so it should be excluded per policy "Voided Amendment Handling". However, the actual spend shows $48,000 for Travel which is $8,000 over budget ($40,000). This is the 20% overrun that needs attention.

The engineering hardware amendment (+$3,000) was pending at the time of the data pull, but the actual spend is $33,500 vs $30,000 budget (11.67% over). Even if that amendment eventually gets applied, it would still be over the 10% threshold.

The marketing advertising line item is 15% over.

All three departments (Engineering, Marketing, Sales) have overruns exceeding the 10% threshold. I've sent emails to the department heads and posted to the finance-alerts Slack channel.

Let me also double-check - the Slack message was sent to channel "CFA" which is the "finance-alerts" channel from the earlier list. That's correct.

All tasks are complete. The reconciliation is done and notifications have been sent.

outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

function.description:
Run a query against QuickBooks Online data.

Args:
    query: SQL-like query string, e.g.
        "SELECT * FROM Invoice WHERE CustomerRef = '123' AND Balance > 0".
        FROM names the entity (Invoice, Bill, Payment, Customer, Vendor,
        Item, Estimate). WHERE supports =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, LIKE, IN, AND,
        OR, NOT and parentheses; nested fields use dots (BillAddr.City) and
        references match their value or name (CustomerRef). ORDER BY,
        STARTPOSITION and MAXRESULTS are honored.

Returns:
    JSON string with QueryResponse records, count returned and total_count.

function.name: gmail_send_email
function.description:
Send an email via Gmail.

Composes and delivers a new outgoing Gmail message to one or more
recipients. Use this to send (not draft) an email — the message is
transmitted immediately and appears in the recipient's inbox. Handles
outbound email dispatch, reply-and-send, forward-and-send, notification
emails, alerts, and any other Gmail send/deliver/transmit action.

Keywords: gmail send email, gmail send mail, gmail compose and send,
send outgoing email, send outbound message, deliver email, transmit
email, dispatch email, email send, gmail sender, mail send, gmail
message send, send a new email, send notification email, send alert
email, email delivery.

Note: this SENDS the email. For drafts use gmail_create_draft instead.

Args:
    to: Recipient email address(es), comma-separated for multiple.
    subject: Email subject line.
    body: Email body content (plain text or HTML).
    cc: CC recipients, comma-separated.
    bcc: BCC recipients, comma-separated.
    from_: Sender email address (alias).
    from_name: Display name for sender.
    reply_to: Reply-to email address.
    body_type: Body format - "plain" or "html" (default: "plain").
    signature: Email signature to append.
    label_ids: Comma-separated label IDs to apply.
    file: File to attach (URL or path).

Returns:
    JSON string confirming the sent message: id, thread_id, subject and
    recipients (the body is not echoed back).

function.name: gmail_find_email
function.description:
Search for emails using Gmail search operators, newest first.

Args:
    query: Gmail search query. Supports operators: from:, to:, cc:,
        subject:, label:, in:, is:unread, is:read, is:starred,
        has:attachment, after:YYYY/MM/DD, before:YYYY/MM/DD, -term, OR,
        and plain text (e.g., "from:user@example.com is:unread"). Terms are
        ANDed; the words AND/OR are operators, not search text.
    id: Message ID for direct lookup (returns single message).
    label: Filter by label (e.g., "INBOX", "SENT").
    max_results: Maximum number of results to return.
    include_spam_trash: Include spam and trash in results.
    format: Email format to return ("full", "metadata", "minimal", "raw").

Returns:
    JSON string with matching messages (newest first), result_count
    returned and total_count matching.

function.name: gmail_get_email_by_id

    JSON string with the message details, or error if not found.

function.name: quickbooks_query
function.description:
Run a query against QuickBooks Online data.

Args:
    query: SQL-like query string, e.g.
        "SELECT * FROM Invoice WHERE CustomerRef = '123' AND Balance > 0".
        FROM names the entity (Invoice, Bill, Payment, Customer, Vendor,
        Item, Estimate). WHERE supports =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, LIKE, IN, AND,
        OR, NOT and parentheses; nested fields use dots (BillAddr.City) and
        references match their value or name (CustomerRef). ORDER BY,
        STARTPOSITION and MAXRESULTS are honored.

Returns:
    JSON string with QueryResponse records, count returned and total_count.

function.name: quickbooks_find_customer
function.description:
Find a customer in QuickBooks Online.

Args:
    where_clause: SQL-like WHERE clause (e.g., "DisplayName = 'John'").
    name: Customer name to search for.
    email: Customer email to search for.

Returns:
    JSON string with found customer or empty result.

function.name: quickbooks_find_payment
function.description:
Find a payment in QuickBooks Online.

Args:
